issues.description: Field 'lectureName' has conflicting types across artifacts: the UML diagram in problem_statement.md declares 'lectureName' as type int, whereas the reference implementation (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java) declares private String lectureName and uses it as text in toString() and other methods. The template code contains the scaffold TODO for adding attributes but the textual examples and tests in the problem description expect a String. This mismatch can confuse students about the correct type to implement (affecting the constructor signature, getters/setters, and toString format).
issues.suggestedFix: Change the UML/type declaration in problem_statement.md so that the lectureName attribute is declared as a String (e.g. '-lectureName: String'). Ensure any places in the problem text or UML showing types reflect String for lectureName and, if present, update the example constructor signature in the description to match the String type and the attribute order from the UML. Optionally review the other UML attribute type annotations for consistency with the solution code.
